card: Exempts private broadcast connections from address-level discouragement and subnet disconnections. When a private broadcast peer misbehaves, it is disconnected immediately without having its address discouraged, and existing private broadcast connections sharing a subnet with another discouraged peer are spared from disconnect. This prevents discouragement behavior from leaking the existence of private broadcast channels or interfering with intentional broadcast connections. Evidence is limited to the author's description.
changed_since_previous: Clarified that in addition to exempting misbehaving private broadcast peers from address discouragement, the patch also prevents subnet discouragement disconnect sweeps from disconnecting co-located private broadcast peers, backed by unit tests in denialofservice_tests.cpp.
evidence: PR description: 'Discouraging a private broadcast connection may be observable. Prevent this by keeping private broadcast connections outside normal discouragement handling. Misbehaving private broadcast peers are still disconnected.'
problem: Subjecting private broadcast connections to normal discouragement handling can make the presence of private broadcast peers externally observable and cause operator-configured private broadcast connections to be dropped if another connection on the same subnet misbehaves.

risk.why: A flaw in misbehavior handling or subnet disconnect logic could inadvertently fail to penalize malicious peers or inappropriately disconnect valid connections.

summary: Exempts private broadcast connections from address-level discouragement and from subnet disconnections triggered by other misbehaving peers. A misbehaving private broadcast peer is still disconnected immediately, but its address is not placed on the discouragement list.
